baseline.goal: The PreToolUse hook `tool/deny.py` refuses a Bash command that sends pytest's output (including `python -m pytest`) through a pipe into another command such as `tail`, `grep` or `head`. The message says to run it again without the pipe, and to use `run_in_background` or `| tee <log file>` for long runs. `| tee`, commands that don't run pytest, and `|` inside quotes still pass. Claude and Codex both get this because both go through `deny.verdict`.
out: Changing the per-project Claude install (`apply.py` writes `permissions.deny` there and does not run `deny.py`); wiring `deny.py` into per-project installs is not part of this change
Changing the existing `enforce.deny` rule matching (the `fnmatchcase` loop) or how rules are declared on the pages
Following nested shells or commands built at runtime (`bash -c "..."`, `eval`, scripts); the existing ponytail note in `deny.py` already says the hook is not a security boundary
Piped runs of test tools other than pytest
done: `deny.verdict({"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "pytest -q | tail -5"}})` returns `permissionDecision: deny`. So do `python -m pytest tool | grep FAIL`, `py -m pytest -x 2>&1 | head` and `cd tool && pytest | tail`
The deny message says to run again without the pipe and names both `run_in_background` and `| tee <log file>` as the ways to handle a long run

These return None: `pytest -q | tee out.log`, `python -m pytest 2>&1 | tee -a log.txt`, `pip install pytest | tail`, `echo "pytest | tail"`, `git commit -m 'pytest | tail'`, `pytest -q`, `pytest -q || echo failed`
The new check runs even when `declared()` returns no deny rules, and the existing declared-rule test (`tool/test_hook.py` around line 139: `sed -i` blocked, `git status` passes) still passes
`codex_pretool.verdict` with a Bash payload `pytest | tail` returns the same deny, shown by a test in `tool/test_codex_hooks.py` or `tool/test_hook.py`
New tests in `tool/test_hook.py` cover every deny and pass case above; `tool/test_hook.py`, `tool/test_codex_hooks.py` and `tool/test_apply.py` all pass

rules: Deny reasons are written in Korean, like the existing `공유 위키의 차단 규칙: ...` message
When the hook hits an error it lets the command through (`hook skipped`); the new check must not raise on commands it can't split, such as unbalanced quotes

decisions.what: Write the pipe check in Python inside `deny.verdict`, not as an `enforce.deny` glob pattern on the pages
decisions.why: An fnmatch pattern like `Bash(*pytest*|*)` can't tell `pip install pytest | tail` or a quoted `|` from a real piped test run, and it can't make an exception for `tee`. The hook has to split the command itself
decisions.rejected: Declaring a `Bash(...)` deny pattern on a page

decisions.what: Split the command into shell words with quotes respected (shlex-style). Cut it into pipeline segments at a lone `|` (and `|&`) and into commands at `&&`, `;` and `||`. Deny when a segment that runs pytest (first word `pytest`, or a python launcher such as `python`/`python3`/`py` followed by `-m pytest`, after any `VAR=value` prefixes) is piped into a next segment whose command is not `tee`
decisions.why: This covers all the allowed cases at once: text in quotes is not a pipe, `||` is not a pipe, `pip install pytest` does not run pytest, and `tee` keeps the output visible while also saving it. Nobody was available to ask, so I settled this rule myself
decisions.rejected: A regex over the raw command string (it breaks on quotes and on `||`)

decisions.what: If the command can't be split (for example, unbalanced quotes), pass it instead of denying
decisions.why: Every other check in this hook lets a command through when it can't judge it. Wrongly blocking a command the hook doesn't understand would cost more than missing one piped test run
decisions.rejected: Denying when the command can't be split

decisions.what: Run the pipe check before the declared-rule loop, so it applies whether or not any page declares deny rules. Leave the per-project Claude wiring as it is
decisions.why: The behaviour is built into the hook, not declared on a page. Making per-project installs run `deny.py` would change how `apply.py` wires hooks and how `keep_denies` works, which is beyond this change. Nobody was available to ask, so I recorded the limit here rather than widening the change
decisions.rejected: Wiring `deny.py` into per-project Claude installs in the same change

deny: 진행이 안 보이게 파이프한 테스트 실행을 거절

## 무엇을 바꿨나

- `pytest`(`-m pytest` 포함)의 출력을 `| tail`, `| grep`, `| head` 처럼 다른 명령으로 넘기면 PreToolUse 훅(`tool/deny.py`)이 거절한다. 그렇게 넘기면 실행이 끝날 때까지 진행 상황이 하나도 안 보이기 때문이다.
- 거절 메시지는 파이프 없이 다시 돌리라고 안내한다. 오래 걸리면 `run_in_background`를 쓰거나 `| tee <로그 파일>` 로 남기면 된다.
- `| tee` 는 허용한다. `pip install pytest | tail` 처럼 실행하지 않는 명령과 따옴표 안의 글자도 허용한다.
- Claude 훅과 Codex 훅(`codex_pretool.py`)이 같은 `deny.verdict`를 쓰므로 둘 다 적용된다.

## 확인

- `tool/test_hook.py` 새 테스트 10개 통과. 훅을 쓰는 테스트(test_hook, test_codex_hooks, test_apply) 54개 통과.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

verify.expected: each of the four commands is denied

verify.expected: `permissionDecisionReason` contains `run_in_background` and `tee`, and says to drop the pipe

verify.item: These return None: `pytest -q | tee out.log`, `python -m pytest 2>&1 | tee -a log.txt`, `pip install pytest | tail`, `echo "pytest | tail"`, `git commit -m 'pytest | tail'`, `pytest -q`, `pytest -q || echo failed`
verify.expected: `deny.verdict` returns None for each (with no declared rule matching them)

verify.expected: a test with `declared` returning no denies still sees `pytest | tail` denied; `test_user_level_claude_carries_no_machine_wide_deny` passes

verify.expected: the test asserts `permissionDecision` `deny` with the pipe message

requirements.text: The pipe check is Python code inside `deny.verdict`; no `Bash(...)` glob pattern is added to any page's `enforce.deny`.

source.locator: decision 1: write the pipe check in Python inside deny.verdict

requirements.text: The command is split into shell words with quotes respected, cut into commands at `&&`, `;` and `||` and into pipeline segments at `|` and `|&`. A segment runs pytest when, after any `VAR=value` prefixes, its first word is `pytest`, or a python launcher (`python`, `python3`, `py`) followed by `-m pytest`. It is denied when such a segment is piped into a next segment whose command is not `tee`.

source.locator: decision 2: shlex-style split and segment rule

invariants: redirections such as `2>&1` on the pytest segment do not change the verdict
`||` is never treated as a pipe

requirements.text: A command that cannot be split (for example, unbalanced quotes) passes the pipe check instead of being denied.

source.locator: decision 3: pass when the command can't be split

failures: a split error (e.g. `ValueError` from shlex) is caught inside the check and the check returns no deny; it does not fall through to the outer `hook skipped` handler

requirements.text: Per-project Claude installs keep their current wiring (`permissions.deny` from `apply.py`, no `deny.py`), so the pipe check reaches them only through installs that already run `deny.py`.

source.locator: decision 4: leave the per-project Claude wiring as it is

requirements.text: A pipe written without spaces, such as `pytest -q|tail -5`, is denied the same way as `pytest -q | tail -5`.

source.locator: follows from decision 2: a lone `|` cuts a segment

postconditions: the splitter treats `|`, `|&`, `||`, `&&` and `;` as operators even without surrounding spaces (e.g. shlex with punctuation_chars), not only as whitespace-separated words

requirements.text: Whether these count as running pytest is not settled: `uv run pytest`, `py -3 -m pytest`, `python3.12 -m pytest`, a path such as `.venv/bin/pytest`, and a path such as `/usr/bin/tee` as the receiving command. Keep the narrow rule in R8 unless widening is clearly cheap, and list whatever is not caught as known gaps in the pull request.
